correctness.rationale: Directly dividing the two positive phase equations yields the unique positive ratio root r=d+sqrt(1+d^2); substitution gives u^2=(h-Q)/r and v^2=r(h-Q). The log-coordinate seasonal map has derivative -tanh z with absolute value <1 everywhere: the two-step map contracts on a compact interval about its established fixed point, proving global convergence from every positive state whenever ab>1. For ab<=1 the even subsequence strictly decreases and can converge only to zero. The exact phase identities yield mean^2=(Q+1)(h-Q)/2 and the factorization (Q-1)(h-Q-2)/2 after comparison with the matched-mean constant-survival equilibrium. At fixed h>3 the one-switch threshold delta=sqrt((h-2)^2-1) is inside persistence delta<sqrt(h^2-1). A standalone standard-library checker reproduced seven exact rational identity cases and 33 high-precision trajectories; none of those finite samples substitutes for the universal analytic proof.
risks: The model assumes multiplicative survival after recruitment, not additive adult survival; changing the operation changes the population equation.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2006 Franke–Yakubu paper gives local small-amplitude signatures and compares 2-cycles with the mean of seasonal carrying capacities. Its §5.5 and Table 2 do not provide the exact all-amplitude mean-survival reference threshold, nor the fixed-mean amplification-to-suppression reversal while both seasons remain individually viable. The 2005 Franke–Yakubu survivor model has additive survival and constant/Beverton–Holt recruitment; its globally monotone framework does not cover the nonmonotone quadratic recruitment map. The relevant published Ricker/Floquet result treats a different nonlinear map and question. An unexamined broader theorem may still imply the identity, so no absolute novelty guarantee is asserted.
residual_risks: The full text of Brauer and Sánchez (2003) was not obtained; a more general older result could potentially subsume the model-specific comparison.
Other specialized periodic-difference-equation sources may imply the algebraic identity even where terminology does not match; this remains for independent literature audit.
No claim of worldwide novelty or verification against unpublished research is made.

value.rationale: Periodic harvesting with matched mean survival fraction is a natural direct comparison in demographic ecological modeling. The exact threshold distinguishes genuine mean-biomass improvement from loss in an overcompensatory model and demonstrates a nonperturbative reversal: at the same mean survival one change in seasonal contrast improves mean abundance and a larger contrast worsens it, without extinguishing the population. Its closed boundary identifies where local-signature intuition ceases to hold, provides explicit globally attracting testbeds for seasonal forcing, and separates persistence from resonance. This is structural mathematical information rather than a routine normalization or arbitrary finite census.
risks: Ecological applicability depends on the quadratic deterministic assumption and a post-recruitment survival mechanism.
Abundance comparison alone does not imply yield, welfare, or management optimality.
